Space exploration has captivated humans for decades. The journey began in the mid-20th century with the space race between the United States and the Soviet Union. This era [[1]] several major accomplishments. In 1961, Yuri Gagarin, a Russian cosmonaut, became the first man to venture into space. Then, in 1969, Neil Armstrong landed on the moon during the epic Apollo 11 mission, delivering the [[2]], “One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.”
Significant breakthroughs like these have been made in space technology, thanks to scientists’ continuous efforts. One example is the establishment of the International Space Station (ISS), which is a microgravity laboratory in space as well as a data center. If it weren’t for the hub, crew members [[3]] research that can only be done in space. Scientists from various countries work collectively aboard it, which helps push the boundaries of human knowledge and prepare humans for future deep space missions.
It’s also worth noting that space travel is [[4]] exclusive to governments. Space tourism has taken off among private citizens. In 2001, American entrepreneur Dennis Tito reportedly paid $20 million to visit the ISS. Since then, 280 people from 23 nations have followed suit and [[5]] their star treks. Perhaps in the near future, touching stars or roaming in the Milky Way won’t be something only existing in fiction!
